question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party and its institutions, with recent personnel appointments such as Cai Qi's expanded roles reinforcing loyalty among elites ahead of the 21st Party Congress expected in late 2027. This congress is widely anticipated to grant him a fourth term as general secretary, extending his leadership at least through 2032, consistent with the pattern established since the 20th Congress in 2022 and the 2018 removal of presidential term limits. No designated successor has emerged, and analyses of Politburo dynamics show limited factional opposition or age-based retirement pressures that could force an earlier transition. Trader consensus at 95.5% for "No" reflects these structural barriers. Sudden health events or internal elite shifts remain the primary variables that could still alter the timeline before 2027.
